meta.title: CarPal admin console (WP15 UI, WP20 admin part; frontend/admin-console/) — build plan and stage log
meta.purpose: Build the internal staff console that operates the platform: Path 2 review approvals, moderation, disputes, verification, privacy requests, plans, flags and the AI kill switch, the USD exchange rate, taxonomy, audit, AI/MCP oversight and analytics. Without it the pilot cannot run without direct API or database work (backend S11 open_after_stage, NI-08).
sources_of_truth: Docs/40.API contract.md (contract 1.2.0) wins for operations, fields, roles and security rules. §23 is the admin plane (62 operations on host admin-api), §2.14 SEC-ADM-1..7.

Docs/23.Admin_WebUI_screens.md wins for screens, layout and UX rules where the contract allows them. Where it asks for data or actions the contract lacks, the gap is recorded in backend_requests (GD-08).
Docs/02.Detailed project plan.md (WP15, WP17, WP20, §1.4, §15) and Docs/90 §9 for scope and hosts.

Cross-plan rule (memory, 2026-11-04): the newer frontend plan wins over backend/dev_plan.json when they disagree; the backend follows. Write ids from other plans with a prefix: 'backend NI-04', 'PWA GD-03'. This plan's ids use the prefix 'ADM' when quoted elsewhere (e.g. 'ADM DI-02').
how_to_use: One stage per working session. Each stage is sized to fit one session (about a 5-hour token budget). If a stage runs long, stop at a task boundary, mark it 'partial' with partial_reason, and continue it as ACn-b next session (as backend S9a/b/c did).
At the start of a stage: read only its context_to_read, then the report of the previous stage (notes_for_next, open_after_stage).

At the end of a stage: set task statuses, fill report (template in conventions.report_template), add new DI/OQ/BR entries, update meta.progress, and run the stage's acceptance commands. Commit only when the user asks.
Backend work that a stage needs (backend_requests with stage 'AC2' or other) is done in backend/ and also logged as a backend stage (S12, S13) in backend/dev_plan.json.

progress.summary: Plan written 2026-11-08 against backend contract 1.2.0 (S1-S11) and the finished PWA (P1-P15). known_state: Since AC2 (backend S12, contract 1.3.0): cp-web-admin is DPoP-bound with private_key_jwt (libs/auth CLIENTS); its key pair is /carpal/config/oauth-admin-client-keys.json on a server (backend/deploy/gen-client-keys.mjs --admin), separate from the PWA's file.
Hosted sign-in: authorize sends every client to <issuer>/signin; the console serves it through its own /id proxy like the PWA (BR-02 not needed).

A staff account without a device-bound passkey answers next 'enrol_passkey' after its password; auth.passkey_enrol_options (emailed code) and auth.passkey_enrol add the first passkey; then next 'mfa' (aal3).

admin.staff_me (GET /v1/admin/me) returns the caller's name, locale, time zone, platform roles and session end. The api host refuses cp-web-admin tokens (audience), so me.get, config.client and the taxonomy reads are not reachable (BR-18).

Staff accounts: backend `pnpm staff:bootstrap` (dev: adm1, adm2, mod1, crv1, sup1 @staff.carpals.test, password carpal-staff-dev-password), `pnpm dev:staff create|list`; on a server backend/deploy/staff-bootstrap.sh with /carpal/config/staff-bootstrap.json.

Dev settings for the console in backend/.env (documented in backend/.env.example): cp-web-admin redirect URIs https://localhost:3200 and :3300 /bff/oauth/callback, CARPAL_WEBAUTHN_RP_ID=localhost, WebAuthn origins http://localhost:3200 and :3300 (plus the PWA's). Production: ADMIN_CONSOLE_HOST in the shared deploy.conf (default admin.<DOMAIN>).

global_decisions.decision: The console is its own Next.js app in frontend/admin-console/ (App Router, TypeScript strict, ESM, Tailwind CSS v4), its own pnpm package (@carpal/admin-console) with its own lockfile, no root workspace. Versions match the PWA so code and fixes move between them: next 16.4.3, react/react-dom 19.3.1, tailwindcss 4.3.3, @tanstack/react-query 5.104.5, zod 4.6.7, i18next 26.4.3, react-i18next 17.0.16, jose 6.2.12, @simplewebauthn/browser 14.0.0, maplibre-gl 6.14.0 (AC9 only), @playwright/test 1.64.1, @axe-core/playwright 4.14.0. Later minor updates are recorded in the stage report.
global_decisions.reason: The admin plane has its own OAuth client (cp-web-admin, aal3, audience admin-api) and must stay reachable only through a gate (SEC-ADM-1; the gate itself is still open, Docs/02 §15). A separate deployable keeps every gate option possible and never ships admin code or routes from the public web.<DOMAIN> origin. Docs/02 §1.4 says admin pages are part of the web app: see DI-01.

global_decisions.decision: Node: run on backend/.tools/node (24.21.0) through tools/use-local-node.sh and .ps1 copied from pwa/tools. .node-version = 24.21.0.

Admin BFF = a copy, with provenance comments, of the framework-free PWA BFF (pwa/src/server/bff: session store port, OAuth client, DPoP, private_key_jwt signer, 1:1 forwarder with registry allowlist, CSRF, header hygiene) under frontend/admin-console/src/server/bff/, adapted for cp-web-admin: acr_values=aal3, audience admin-api, access 5 min, refresh 30 min idle, 8 h absolute, allowlist = admin-api routes + the api-host reads in GD-07. No guest/anonymous tokens and no cp-ssr. When the business web app (cp-web-portal) starts, the three copies are extracted to one shared package (recommendation R-01).
global_decisions.reason: Reuse what already passed the strict-mode checks in PWA P15 without touching the live PWA now; extract once there are three users (rule of three).

global_decisions.decision: Staff sign-in (A-AUTH-01) is hosted by the console itself at /id/* on the admin host, not by the PWA. Only what staff need: email + password, then a passkey (WebAuthn) for aal3; no sign-up, no SMS code, no social sign-in. A staff account without a passkey is taken through a forced passkey enrolment after password + email code, then signs in again at aal3. Needs the backend to choose the sign-in URL per client (BR-02) and to finish staff WebAuthn end to end (BR-03).
global_decisions.reason: Keeps staff credentials and the staff flow off the public consumer app and behind the same gate as the console; A-AUTH-01 differs from the consumer sign-in in almost every rule. Override with OQ-01.
global_decisions.amendment_2026_11_09: OQ-01 answered: sign-in on the console's own pages. As built in AC2 (backend S12): the console's /id proxy serves <issuer>/signin (no per-client URL, BR-02). Steps: email + password, then for an account without a device-bound passkey an emailed code and the passkey enrolment, then the passkey (aal3). Only device-bound credentials count (security key or a non-synced platform passkey; SEC-ADM-2); a one-time code alone never opens enrolment. A passkey-only sign-in (auth.webauthn_options purpose signin) also reaches aal3 with a device-bound key.

global_decisions.decision: EN and FA with full RTL. The locale comes from the staff member's me.locale (switchable in the avatar menu, kept in a cookie); no locale segment in URLs (internal app, no SEO). Common keys come from shared/i18n/locales; console strings go in an 'admin' namespace following the PWA layout (pwa/src/lib/i18n), and the key-parity check covers it. Dates: Jalali in FA and Gregorian in EN, stored and sent in UTC; digits localised for display only; IDs, codes and timestamps in tables can switch to Latin digits.

Design: shared/design-system/web tokens, fonts and components, synced with a copy of pwa/tools/sync-design-system.mjs; the PWA's ported components (pwa/src/components/ds) are copied as the starting kit. The console adds a dense admin layer: data table, three-panel case layout, drawer, reason panel, masked field, four-eyes banner, entity chip, timeline. Logical CSS properties only (copy of pwa/tools/check-logical-css.mjs). Light and dark themes. An environment badge (DEV / STAGING / PROD in red) is always visible.
global_decisions.amendment_2026_11_09: OQ-12 answered: the environment badge label is always the Latin DEV / STAGING / PROD (lang="en"), in both languages; only the screen-reader hint is translated.

global_decisions.decision: API scope: the console calls the 62 admin-api operations of contract 1.2.0 through its BFF. A short, explicit list of api-host reads may be forwarded as well if the cp-web-admin token is accepted there (checked in AC2): me.get (staff identity and roles), config.client, taxonomy reads for the tree. Anything else is reached by opening the public page (pwa.<DOMAIN>) in a new tab, never by widening the BFF.
global_decisions.amendment_2026_11_09: Checked in AC2: the api host refuses every cp-web-admin token (it verifies the api audience; PUB reads also need a token of that audience). The api-read list is empty; staff identity comes from admin.staff_me (contract 1.3.0). The reads still needed from the api host (taxonomy tree in AC12, region map settings in AC9) are BR-18 / OQ-13.

global_decisions.decision: The contract wins over Docs/23. A screen ships with what the contract provides; missing data or actions are recorded as backend_requests (BR-xx) and as doc issues, and are built in AC14 only if the user approves them (OQ-07). Buttons for actions that do not exist are not shown (no dead buttons).
global_decisions.reason: The backend is finished and swept; the console must not invent endpoints.

global_decisions.decision: Staff roles are the contract's four: ADM platform_admin, MOD platform_moderator, SUP platform_support, CRV platform_community_reviewer. Navigation and buttons are shown from the role sets in each operation's sec: line (generated into a role table at AC1). Docs/23's nine roles map as: Content moderator, Verification officer, Trust & Safety lead → MOD (lead powers that need ADM are shown only to ADM); Community reviewer → CRV; Privacy officer, AI governance, Commercial admin, Platform admin → ADM; Support agent → SUP. The server always decides; the UI only hides.

Purpose-bound reads (SEC-ADM-5): every PURP read is opened from a work item (case, dispute, DSR, verification, review approval). The purpose travels in the URL (?purpose=<kind>:<id>) and the BFF sends it as CarPal-Access-Purpose. Opening a person or organization without a work item asks the staff member to pick or open one. A-USR-01 is therefore an exact lookup (one identifier), not a browsable list (DI-03).

Every mutating action opens the reason panel (reason code + note; note required for removals, suspensions and rejections) and sends the reason as the contract asks (body 'reason', or the CarPal-Reason header on DELETE). A 202 PendingChange (4EYES) shows 'Waiting for a second staff member' with a link to Pending approvals; SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN is explained, not shown as an error. Operations tagged AAL3 or STEP_UP trigger a re-authentication with the passkey and replay the action.
global_decisions.reason: SEC-ADM-2, SEC-ADM-3, SEC-ADM-6; Docs/23 principles 1 and 7.

global_decisions.decision: No personal data is stored in the browser: TanStack Query cache in memory only, cleared on sign-out, idle timeout and staff switch; no localStorage/sessionStorage/IndexedDB for responses; Cache-Control: no-store on every page and BFF response; no service worker; no analytics or error-reporting SDK; console logs never print response bodies. Saved views and column choices (no data) may be kept in localStorage.
Ports: dev 3200, e2e 3300, both over https://localhost with the PWA's dev certificate approach. Backend lite: admin-api :8081, auth :8082.
global_decisions.amendment_2026_11_09: OQ-11 answered: every page in production (and staging) opens over https only: env.ts refuses an http CARPAL_ADMIN_ORIGIN outside dev, pages send HSTS outside dev (AC2), and nginx answers port 80 with a redirect (AC11). Dev (3200) and E2E (3300) run over http://localhost like the PWA, with the https redirect URI brought back by the /id proxy.

global_decisions.decision: Tests: Vitest unit and DOM projects; integration project against the live lite backend; Playwright E2E (Chromium) with a CDP virtual authenticator for passkeys; @axe-core/playwright for accessibility; RTL screenshots for key screens. `pnpm check` = lint + logical-css + typecheck + unit + contract:check + i18n:check + ds:check.
global_decisions.reason: Same quality bar as the PWA (P13).

global_decisions.decision: Deployment: frontend/admin-console/deploy/ (deploy.md, admin-setup.sh, admin-update.sh, lib.sh, templates/) following the WinSCP + staging-folder workflow and the shared /carpal/config/deploy.conf; ADMIN_HOST=admin.<DOMAIN> derived from DOMAIN; scripts LF-only. The access gate in front of the console is a setting (ADMIN_GATE=ip_allowlist | none), default ip_allowlist, because the final access strategy is still open (Docs/02 §15, OQ-02).
global_decisions.reason: Memory: deploy workflow and host naming; SEC-ADM-1.

global_decisions.decision: Order of stages follows pilot value: foundation and sign-in first, then the settings that unblock the pilot (exchange rate, flags, plans), then the queues the pilot depends on (Path 2 approvals, moderation, verification, privacy), then deploy (milestone M1), then taxonomy, oversight and analytics, contract gaps and closure.
global_decisions.reason: Backend S11 open_after_stage lists the missing admin console as a pilot blocker for moderation, Path 2 approvals, data requests and the exchange rate.

code_rules: No widening: the BFF forwards only allowlisted operations 1:1 (SEC-WEB-1).
Every action button is gated by the generated role table and hidden when the caller lacks the role; server errors 403 still render the no-permission state.
Unknown enum values from the server render as 'Unknown (<value>)', never crash (PWA P13 rule).
Masked by default: phone, email, full name, VIN, plate, documents. Reveal = purpose-bound read, logged by the backend.
Removals and suspensions are never bulk (Docs/23 §3.3).

report.summary: The admin BFF and the typed client. Staff sign in through /bff/login → the console origin's /id proxy → the auth host (password, emailed code and passkey enrolment the first time, device-bound passkey at aal3) → /bff/oauth/callback, which exchanges the code with private_key_jwt and a DPoP proof, demands aal3 and a staff profile from admin.staff_me, and rotates the session. The browser holds only __Host-cpa_sid; tokens, the DPoP key and the profile stay server-side. The forwarder passes exactly the 63 admin-api operations of the generated map, with CSRF on writes, the purpose of PURP reads and the reason header of DELETEs. Sessions idle out after 30 min and end after 8 h. Step-up (/bff/reauth) requires a fresh sign-in by the same staff member and can carry a saved action. The browser client maps problems (step-up, separation of duties, version preconditions, missing purpose) and tells applied, four-eyes-pending and background-job outcomes apart; its cache is memory-only and cleared on sign-out, session end and staff switch.

deviations_log.summary: Console strings in the console's own src/lib/i18n/locales ('admin' namespace), shared common/format read from @carpal/i18n.
Generated types.ts picks from @carpal/api-contracts instead of a second full copy; contract:check verifies the shared package's registry sha.
Three themes (Daylight, Sunlight, Night) instead of light/dark.
Cookies cpa_locale / cpa_theme (not the PWA's names) because localhost cookies are shared across ports.
Full nonce CSP with Trusted Types in AC1 instead of a stub; AC3.T6 becomes a review plus BFF/API route headers.
Dev and E2E over http://localhost like the PWA, not https (GD-13); decision in OQ-11.
Later-stage dependencies installed now to lock GD-01 versions; maplibre-gl waits for AC9.
AC2 also changed the console and the PWA (contract 1.3.0 regenerated everywhere; OQ-11, OQ-12 applied).
BR-02 not built: the /id proxy serves <issuer>/signin.
The new passkey is proven in the same interaction instead of a second full sign-in.
Strict mode warns instead of refusing to start without the cp-web-admin key.
The cp-web-admin key pair has its own file (the PWA reads its key file whole).
Contract 1.3.0 (minor) instead of a 1.2.1 patch; AC14 becomes contract 1.4.0.
GD-07 api reads removed: the api host refuses admin tokens.
Route adapter src/app/api/[...path] instead of api/v1/admin/[...path]: every /api path gets the BFF's 404 problem+json and headers (Next.js's 404 page would answer the others).
Cookies __Host-cpa_sid / __Host-cpa_iar instead of the PWA's names (localhost shares cookies across ports); the session cookie is always a browser-session cookie (no "Keep me signed in" for staff).

Step-up uses prompt=login without max_age (the auth host's authorize takes none); the callback checks auth_time and the same sub. Actions survive the step-up through /bff/intents (copied from the PWA).

PURPOSE_REQUIRED is a client code (the backend answers 400 MALFORMED_REQUEST); the BFF refuses a malformed purpose with 400 reason purpose. "PRECONDITION_FAILED" = the contract's VERSION_MISMATCH 412 and PRECONDITION_REQUIRED 428.
The ASYNC helper is a generic pollUntil(): contract 1.3.0 has no admin-plane job read (DI-14, BR-20).
Only API calls and sign-in count as activity; /bff/session reads and token refreshes do not. The absolute end is the earlier of 8 h and admin.staff_me session_expires_at.
Every callback demands aal3 and a staff profile for the same sub (admin.staff_me with a role); otherwise the new tokens are revoked (?signin=step_up|not_staff).
Outside dev the env requires strict mode and the cp-web-admin key; unlike the PWA it allows the lite session store in prod (one process; sessions end on restart). AC11 decides.

Sign-in pages: one /id/signin page whose steps (password, key, first-key enrolment, paused, expired, gate, forgot password) are client state, as the PWA does, plus /id/signed-out; not separate /id/passkey, /id/enrol-passkey, /id/locked, /id/disabled, /id/expired pages (folder_layout). Keeps the interaction and the typed email between steps.

No 'account disabled' state of its own: the auth host answers disabled staff accounts with the same INVALID_CREDENTIALS as a wrong password (SEC-AU-11), so the generic message names that case ('If your staff account was disabled, ask a platform admin').

Navigation: the Docs/23 §3.1 sections without operations in contract 1.3.0 (Featured placements, Notifications & templates, Policies & consent texts, Support) are not listed (GD-08); 'MCP & Audit' is two sections (MCP clients, Audit log); Pending approvals and Exchange rates are added. 20 sections in four groups (work, records, oversight, settings).

No-permission and not-found are states the console page renders inside the shell (status 200), not forbidden()/notFound() (403/404): in Next.js 16.4.3 either one thrown by a page escapes the server render, the response is an empty <html id="__next_error__"> shell drawn on the client, and the enforced Trusted Types CSP blocks that draw (no 'default' policy without the root layout's head): a blank page. The server still refuses every call the role may not make.

BFF and page additions for the shell: /bff/session carries server_time (the idle warning measures against the server clock); the callback sets cpa_locale from admin.staff_me locale when the browser has no choice (GD-05); the proxy passes x-carpal-path and lets ui_locales choose the sign-in language; CSP worker-src 'self' for the proof-of-work worker (was 'none').

An app icon (src/app/icon.svg, the PWA's car glyph on Metal black) and a 404 for file-like paths in the console layout: the browser's own /favicon.ico request matched the [section] route and started a second sign-in, which replaced the auth host's interaction cookie and made the first sign-in answer 'expired'.

recommendations_for_next_stages.text: When the business web app (cp-web-portal) starts, extract the BFF core (session, oauth, dpop, private_key_jwt, forwarder, csrf), the typed client and the design-system kit from pwa/ and frontend/admin-console/ into shared packages instead of making a third copy.
Ask the WP0 owner to settle the staff permission matrix (DI-02) and the four-eyes list (OQ-04) before AC14, so the backend roles and the Docs/23 roles match.
Run backend NI-02 (purpose bound to the record, BR-09) before real staff use the console with real user data.

The console now depends on shared/ (api-contracts generated by the PWA, i18n common/format, design-system web copy). Whenever shared/ or the backend contract changes, run in this order: `pnpm contract:generate` in pwa/, then `pnpm contract:generate` and `pnpm check` in frontend/admin-console. A small root script (or CI job) that runs both apps' checks would make this automatic (DI-11).

Plan the pilot's staff accounts before AC6 (OQ-10): two ADM accounts are needed for any ADM-only four-eyes change (kill switch off, a rate change over 20 %, plans, retention, role grants), plus at least one MOD and one CRV. The first ADM comes from the AC11.T3 runbook; the second must be granted by four-eyes, so create both before the four-eyes rule matters (backend bootstrap or the dev tool in dev).

AC3 can be smaller than planned: security headers (D-05), the operation map with roles, reason/purpose/4EYES/ETAG/IDEM/ASYNC/AAL3 flags, and the route allowlist source (src/lib/api/generated/operations.ts) are ready. The forwarder should build its allowlist straight from ADMIN_OPERATIONS (method + path template + host), never from a hand-written list.

Order security keys for the pilot staff now (OQ-14 default: two per person, FIDO2 with USB-C/NFC), or check that each staff PC has Windows Hello. Phone passkeys usually sync and are refused for staff.
Build BR-19 (staff passkey management, ADM reset with four-eyes) before the pilot, so a spare key can be registered and a lost key does not need SQL on the server.
Decide OQ-13 before AC9 and build BR-18 as a small backend stage with it (admin-api reads for the taxonomy tree and region map settings, contract 1.4.0 together with any AC14 items that are ready).

At the next PWA stage run its pnpm test:int and pnpm e2e once against the backend at contract 1.3.0 (AC2 changed only generated types, three version strings and one template list in pwa/, checked by its unit tests, lint and contract:check).

Put the integration-test settings of README "Integration tests" into backend/.env (or a small script) so pnpm test:int of the console and of the PWA run against one strict backend without hand-set variables; the console test creates one ADM account per run in the dev database (bff-int-…@staff.carpals.test), harmless but visible in `pnpm dev:staff list`.

Three BFF copies now share most code (PWA, console, later the portal): extract them when cp-web-portal starts (R-01). The console copy differs in config, session lifetimes and cookies, the aal3/staff checks of the callback, the allowlist source and the purpose/reason headers; everything else (crypto, csrf, http, dpop, token client, redis, auth proxy) is the same.

PWA: check its notFound() pages in the production build (pnpm e2e on :3100). The PWA's P3 note says the not-found body is drawn on the client; under the enforced Trusted Types CSP the console found that draw blocked (blank page, D-26). If the PWA shows the same, render the not-found state in the page there too, or give the error shell a policy.

Pilot staff onboarding note: the first sign-in asks for the password, a code from the work email and the security key in one go; have the key at hand and the mailbox open. Phone passkeys that sync are refused (SEC-ADM-2).

E2E accounts pile up in the dev database (bff-int-… and e2e-…@staff.carpals.test, one per test). A backend `pnpm dev:staff prune --domain staff.carpals.test --prefix e2e-` (dev only) would keep `pnpm dev:staff list` readable.
